title: FIXP-hardness of exact Hylland–Zeckhauser equilibrium
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Is computing an exact Hylland–Zeckhauser equilibrium for a one-sided matching market FIXP-hard under the standard FIXP reductions?
definitions: There are equally many agents and unit-supply goods with explicitly given nonnegative rational utilities. Each agent has budget one and consumes a lottery totaling one unit. At equilibrium the lotteries clear the market and maximize each agent’s expected utility subject to budget and unit-demand constraints. Exact equilibrium coordinates may be irrational. FIXP is the class of fixed-point search problems defined by algebraic circuits with rational constants and the standard arithmetic/max/min operations.

context_blocks.text: The Hylland–Zeckhauser market turns random assignment into a pricing equilibrium with fairness and efficiency properties. Exact equilibrium is known to belong to FIXP, while approximation is PPAD-complete.

The source explicitly leaves exact FIXP-hardness open. This is not the already established hardness of approximate equilibrium, nor a claim that every exact output can be written as a short rational vector. An exact classification would identify the real-algebraic difficulty of this central assignment mechanism.

why: Complete the exact complexity classification of an influential market mechanism with irrational equilibria.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
